questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience a different culture and a different education system. I chose University of Queensland because Brisbane seemed like a nice city and the academic level of the University seemed relatively high.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university did a great job providing all necessary information, so it was quite easy to find the needed information. There was a Zoom session prior to arrival with a lot of information and the opportunity to ask for any information not presented by the university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got assistance with my courses, as one of my courses got cancelled when i got there. The university was very helpful with providing a list of courses suitable for exchange students, and they helped me with enrolment in a new course.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to find accomodation outside of campus, but most of it were in student complexes. It was quite hard to find shared houses, as there wasn't a lot on offer compared to how many people were searching. I ended up staying in a student complex, which was alright, but I would have liked to live in a shared house, which is a lot cheaper than living in a student complex.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very nice to live off campus. The public transportation is quite good, so it is pretty easy to get to the university from most of the city. I would recommend looking for a place in either West End, South Bank or the CBD.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I did most of the course registration online, and then I just had to enrol in the courses when I got there.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of possibility to get help available. The student central at campus offered help with course registration and enrolment as well as any other difficulties with course enrolment.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses i registrered for except for one, which got cancelled. I got another course instead, which I really liked, so I was quite happy with my courses in general.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about course registration. It is quite easy to change courses after arriving in Brisbane. I would just make sure to get preapproval for as many courses as possible in advance to be able to freely change courses after arrival.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were not as hard and demanding as the courses from the University of Copenhagen. I didn't have to put in as much effort to succeed, as I would have at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching were quite different. A lot of courses were intensive and thus the teaching only lasted a few weeks. Additionally, I didn't have any regular exams, as all courses finished with a written assignment (academic paper).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Maritime Law
Mediation and Conflict Management
Fundamentals of the Common Law
International Law and Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All my courses were good and suitable for exhange students, as they didn't require any prior knowledge to the Australian legal system and the common law system. I enjoyed Maritime Law the most, as it was the course resembling courses from the University of Copenhagen the most.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to go buy kitchen equipment, as it was not in my apartment, when I got it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries was way more expensive than I expected. Transportation was quite cheap compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of clubs available. They were all presenting their club at market day during orientation week. It was a great opportunity to find activities to parcipate in during the exchange.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of clubs, and I would just recommend finding a club within your area of interest. There is a club for almost everything, so there is plenty of opportunity to find something of interest.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would just recommend traveling a lot. Plan some longer trips during the holidays. There is a lot of places close to Brisbane, where you can go in the weekends, so there is plenty of opportunity to experience Australia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes. Australia is very Western, so the it is quite easy to adjust to the local culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There is a lot of social activities during the first couple of weeks, which I would highly recommend attending. After that I would just recommend staying in touch with the all the people you meet, as it is a lot harder to meet new people later on in the semester.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There wasn't any significant cultural differences. The most challenging differences I encountered was probably when I traveled to places with a high population of aboriginals, as their culture is quite a bit different.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their laid back and welcoming attitude.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Travel a lot. There will be plenty of time, if the academics is planned well. 
Join some clubs. It is a good way to meet people.
Attend as many social activities as possible during the first couple of weeks.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The opportunity to travel a lot in a very nice and diverse country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding the time to do everything i wanted to do while in Australia.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
